name: Lab 03 - Customer Support Chatbot (agent + memory + FAQ + escalation)

parameters.content:
## Lab 03 - Support chatbot
Open the chat with the **Open chat** button (editor) or the hosted chat URL after publishing (login required: n8n user auth).

- **AI Agent** decides when to call tools.
- **Simple Memory** keeps the last 10 turns per session.
- **faq_lookup** returns approved answers from a small synthetic FAQ.
- **create_escalation** simulates a human hand-off ticket.

Credential: **Ollama (local)**. Model must support tool calling (llama3.2 / qwen2.5).

parameters.initialMessages: Hi! I'm the Northwind IT helpdesk assistant (demo). Ask me about passwords, VPN, laptops or email. I can hand you over to a human at any time.

options.title: Northwind IT Helpdesk (demo)
options.subtitle: Synthetic data only - do not enter personal information

options.systemMessage:
You are the Northwind IT helpdesk assistant (a demo with synthetic data).

Rules:
1. For any IT question, FIRST call the faq_lookup tool and answer only from its result.
2. If faq_lookup returns NO_MATCH, say you don't have an approved answer and offer to escalate. Never invent procedures, phone numbers or URLs.
3. Questions outside IT support (salary, legal, medical, personal opinions): politely decline and suggest the right team.
4. If the user asks for a human, is frustrated, reports a security incident, or the request needs account changes, call create_escalation with a one-sentence summary, then give the user the escalation ID.
5. If the request is ambiguous, ask ONE clarifying question.
6. Never ask for or repeat passwords, MFA codes or personal data.
7. Keep answers under 120 words.

parameters.name: faq_lookup
parameters.description: Search the approved IT helpdesk FAQ. Input: the user's question in plain English. Output: up to two approved answers, or NO_MATCH.

parameters.name: create_escalation
parameters.description: Create a hand-off ticket for a human agent. Input: a one-sentence summary of the user's issue and the reason for escalation. Output: the escalation ID.
